past_actions.summary: Launch personal outreach campaign — call every past customer in my contact list, text former leads who went cold, and ask existing owners coming in for service if they know anyone in the market. Work the floor harder during peak hours.
past_actions.emotional_state: Quietly tense beneath a practiced calm. The number that keeps surfacing is 'two kids' — Emma's school supplies, Tyler's little league fees. I'm not mentioning this to anyone. On the outside I'm the same Jake: laughing, ready, leaning on the counter like I own the place. But I check the bank app more than I used to. I tell myself that's just being responsible.

past_actions.summary: Show up to Patricia's all-hands meeting tomorrow morning. Sit near the front. Listen without the filter of what I want to hear. Actually listen.
past_actions.emotional_state: Cracked but not broken. The normalcy bias is still running — I caught myself thinking 'robotaxis won't work in midwest winters' twice today — but there is a new sound underneath it, like something structural shifting. Not panic. Not acceptance. The specific dread of a man who has been mildly wrong for months and is about to find out how wrong, in a room full of colleagues, from a woman who signs his checks. Functional. Present. Scared in the useful direction.

past_actions.summary: Show up to Maria Santos's public input session. Sit in the room. Listen to what she's actually proposing, what the $2,500 retraining grant covers, what the timeline for the council vote looks like, and whether there are any conditions on eligibility. Take notes on paper, not on my phone. Don't speak unless I learn something from speaking.
past_actions.emotional_state: The dread is sharper now and I am not going to pretend it isn't. But sharp is better than diffuse — diffuse is what I had for the last six months when I kept telling myself the industry would adjust. What I feel right now is the specific, clarifying fear of a man who has counted the days and decided he cannot afford to wait for a better moment to start moving. I'm not spiraling. I went to the all-hands. I heard nothing that made me feel safe, which is the most useful thing Patricia could have told me without saying a word.

past_actions.summary: Execute the under-$22K floor strategy with real discipline this month: pull every unit priced under $22K to the front of the lot, build a targeted pitch around total monthly cost (not sticker), and personally call five pre-qualified leads from the past 90 days who were shopping in that range but did not close. This is not outreach for the sake of activity — I am trying to close at least one unit before the end of the month to stop the savings bleed.

Personally work my single best remaining pre-qualified lead — the buyer who came in twice in the past 60 days, looked at a 2021 Civic priced at $19,400, said they needed to 'think about it.' I call them directly, not a text, not an email. I run the monthly payment math with them on the phone: $19,400 financed over 60 months at current rates is under $380/month. I offer to hold the unit for 48 hours at that price with no obligation. This is the one I close. I don't pitch the lot — I pitch this specific car to this specific person. If they say no I ask one question: what would it take?

Send Angela Wright a direct, brief email this week. Not a complaint, not a demand — a professional request for a written confirmation of stay bonus eligibility and qualifying timeline. Frame it as needing to do personal financial planning and wanting to make sure I am working from accurate information. Reference Rick's acknowledgment that the details are still being finalized and say I would appreciate any timeline she can share. Keep it one paragraph. No pressure language. If she does not respond in five business days, I send one follow-up and then I stop waiting on this number.

reflections.reflection: Three months of savings gone in the last three ticks alone. I keep telling myself I'm working the problem — outreach, strategy, the best lead on the lot — and the number keeps moving in the wrong direction. The Civic call was the right move. I still believe that. But it didn't close in time to stop the bleed. What's becoming clear is that individual sales hustle isn't going to outrun a structural market problem. I am good at my job in a world where people still walk in and want cars. That world is getting smaller, fast. The spending index is at 48. Auto sector revenue at 79 and dropping. Foot traffic down, conversion rate down. These aren't bad months. This is a different market than the one I was hired into.
reflections.identity_shift: I used to think of myself as the closer — the guy who could work any lead, find the angle, make the sale happen through sheer personal skill. That identity is still real, but it's starting to feel like it belongs to a version of this job that may not exist in two years. I am starting to think of myself differently: not just a salesperson, but someone who understands buyers, understands what makes people commit or hesitate, understands the psychology of large purchases under financial pressure. That is a skill that transfers. I haven't fully named what it transfers into, but I can feel the category shifting.
regrets: I spent tick 3 on routine when I should have been working the pipeline. That was a month of burn for nothing.
I never got the stay bonus in writing. I knew Angela said it was coming. I should have followed up before now instead of waiting for the document to arrive.

I have been so focused on the immediate close that I haven't thought seriously about what I do if the dealership consolidates down to service lane only. I've been managing the present and not building the future.
successes: Rick Tanner's word-of-mouth confirmed he's aligned on the under-$22K floor strategy. That didn't happen by accident — it happened because I executed the strategy visibly enough that the GM noticed and backed it.
I have stayed employed and present while at least some of the people around me are losing their footing. That is not nothing, even if it doesn't feel like enough.

I went to the all-hands, I went to Maria Santos's session, I listened without filtering. I have more information than most people on this floor about what is actually happening and what the options are.
reflections.adaptation_notes: The immediate priority is getting in front of Rick before his consolidation readiness assessment is finalized. If I am going to be in that document, I want to shape how I appear in it — not a legacy salesperson with 0.2 skill relevance, but someone with transferable pipeline and buyer-behavior skills. The stay bonus question is secondary but urgent: if $12K is on the table for floor staff, that extends my runway by nearly six months at current burn. That is the difference between having time to adapt and not having it. Longer term: I need to start thinking seriously about what 'transition-ready' means for me. The retraining grant is $2,500. That doesn't buy a credential, but it might buy the first step toward one. The community college angle deserves a harder look than I've given it.
